title: Coherent cotangent truncation for Noetherian schemes
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with $X,Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Use the Zariski sheaf standard polynomial cotangent complex $L=L_{X/Y}$ [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Good truncation $N=\tau_{\geq-1}L$ means replacing degree $-1$ by the cokernel of the differential from degree $-2$, retaining degrees $\geq0$ and discarding lower degrees. The complex $L$ has no positive-degree cohomology. The object $N$ has coherent cohomology sheaves, zero outside degrees $-1,0$, and $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Locally a presentation $R\to P\twoheadrightarrow A$, with $P$ a finite polynomial $R$-algebra and kernel $J$, identifies $N$ in the derived category with $[\widetilde{J/J^2}\to\widetilde{\Omega^1_{P/R}\otimes_PA}]$ in degrees $-1,0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$ in degree zero and $j=0,1$, precomposition with $L\to N$ is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(N,G[j])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(L,G[j]).$$
The truncation and these maps commute with restriction to opens. No claim is made that $L$ itself has no cohomology below degree $-1$.

source.place: Tag 08UW (lemma-compare-cotangent-complex-with-naive-ringed-spaces); more-morphisms.tex Tags 0D0I (lemma-NL-affine), 0D0J (lemma-netherlander-quasi-coherent), 0D0K (lemma-netherlander-fp). Ext comparison from the truncation triangle and standard t-structure orthogonality, as used in Tag 08UZ.

proof.text: Use the actual standard sheaf complex in [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison]. Its simplicial degree $n$ is placed in cochain degree $-n$ and there are zero positive terms, so $H^i(L)=0$ for $i>0$. Its good truncation $N$ therefore has only degrees $-1,0$: degree $-1$ is the incoming cokernel and degree $0$ is unchanged. The cohomology formula for good truncation gives $H^i(N)=H^i(L)$ for $i\geq-1$ and zero for $i<-1$.

Choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$ with $f(U)\subset V$. The ring map $R\to(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)(U)$ and the section maps of [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] give $L_{A/R}\to L(U)$. The tilde/global-sections adjunction, applied degreewise, gives $\widetilde{L_{A/R}}\to L|_U$. At $x\in U$ with primes $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\mathfrak q\subset R$ this is the canonical map $L_{A/R}\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p}\to L_{A_{\mathfrak p}/R_{\mathfrak q}}$: the tilde stalk formula gives its source, and the cotangent stalk formula gives its target, using the inverse-image stalk isomorphism and the affine structure-sheaf stalk formula to identify $(f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y)_x=R_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{X,x}=A_{\mathfrak p}$. The localization assertion of [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] says precisely that this map is a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness and detection of exactness by module stalks then show that the sheaf map is a quasi-isomorphism. All these maps are induced by the same section maps and hence commute with further restriction.

For any polynomial presentation $R\to P\twoheadrightarrow A$ with kernel $J$, apply [lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model] to get $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{A/R}\simeq C(P)=[J/J^2\to\Omega^1_{P/R}\otimes_PA]$. The associated-sheaf functor preserves kernels by [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits] and cokernels by the colimit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. It therefore preserves the kernel/image/quotient defining cohomology and the cokernel defining good truncation. Applying it to the ring comparison and using step 2 yields $N|_U\simeq[\widetilde{J/J^2}\to\widetilde{\Omega^1_{P/R}\otimes_PA}]$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$. This is the derived comparison, not merely an identification of its cohomology modules.

Choose the affine neighbourhoods in the definition of locally finite presentation: $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, so $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. The classes of the $g_i$ generate $J/J^2$ over $A$: changing a coefficient by an element of $J$ changes its product with $g_i$ by an element of $J^2$. By the polynomial differential formula (with intermediate algebra $R$), $\Omega^1_{P/R}\otimes_PA\simeq A^n$, since $\Omega^1_{R/R}=0$ by the universal derivation definition. Thus both modules in step 3 are finite over $A$. Their associated sheaves are quasi-coherent and of finite type by the tilde-sections and affine finite-type assertions.

source.place: Tag 0D0K (lemma-netherlander-fp), explicit finite generators; algebra.tex Tag 00RX

proof.text: Every open $U$ used above is locally Noetherian, since $X$ is. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], both associated sheaves in step 3 are coherent. Their kernel and cokernel are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]; these are exactly $H^{-1}(N)|_U$ and $H^0(N)|_U$. Coherence is local directly from its definition: at a point choose such a $U$, and test the finite generators and finite-type kernels after further restriction inside $U$. Hence the two global cohomology sheaves are coherent. Finally $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent (locally $\widetilde A$) and generated by $1$, so the same finite-type criterion makes it coherent.

Put $T=\tau_{\leq-2}L$. The canonical truncation triangle is $T\to L\xrightarrow{q}N\to T[1]$ by [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] with $b=-1$. We have $T\in D^{\leq-2}$, $T[1]\in D^{\leq-3}$, and $G[j]\in D^{\geq-j}$ for $j=0,1$ under the shift convention of the standard t-structure. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T,G[j])=\operatorname{Hom}(T[1],G[j])=0$, since $-2<-j$ and $-3<-j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact]: every $L\to G[j]$ factors through $q$ because its composite with $T\to L$ is zero; two such factorizations differ by a map $N\to G[j]$ factoring through $T[1]$, hence by zero. Therefore precomposition by $q$ is bijective, and is an isomorphism of abelian groups since composition is additive.

For an open inclusion $j:W\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact] gives exact restriction of module sheaves. Termwise restriction therefore preserves the kernels and cokernels in good truncation and the kernel/image/quotient in cohomology; hence it preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces a functor on the derived categories. It identifies $j^{-1}N$ with $\tau_{\geq-1}(j^{-1}L)$, including the quotient map $j^{-1}q$, while [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] identifies $j^{-1}L$ with the cotangent complex for the restricted morphism. For $a:N\to G[j]$, restriction sends $a\circ q$ to $(a|_W)\circ(q|_W)$. This proves the commuting square of Hom restriction maps and the isomorphisms of step 6. An arbitrary $G$ is allowed; no coherence or flatness of $G$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q127-b18918fae (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS. The delivery is a seven-step split with no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and agree with Stacks 08UW (canonical map L→NL identifying τ_{≥-1}L) and 0D0I/0D0K (locally a two-term complex in the finitely presented case). Step checks: (1) is elementary, from def-kun-truncations with n=-1. (2) builds the affine map tilde(L_{A/R})→L|_U and checks it on stalks; the stalks are L_{A_p/R_q} by the inverse-image stalk lemma and clause (1) of spec-domain-stalks (the domain clause is not used); the localization clause applies because R∖q maps into A∖p; module-stalk-exact detects quasi-isomorphisms. (3) uses lci-naive-cotangent-model, which has no lci hypothesis and allows any polynomial P, and tilde is exact, so the result is a derived zig-zag and not only an identification of cohomology. (4) the classes of the g_i generate J/J^2 and Ω_{P/R}⊗A≅A^n by the polynomial-extension lemma with Ω_{R/R}=0. (5) uses the locally Noetherian coherence criterion and coherent kernel/cokernel closure, and coherence is local. (6) uses the truncation triangle with b=-1: the bounds T∈D^{≤-2}, T[1]∈D^{≤-3}, G[j]∈D^{≥-j} with j≤1 give the vanishing, and hom-out-of-triangle (i)/(ii) give surjectivity and injectivity. (7) uses exact restriction to opens. Edge cases tested: identity, polynomial algebra, closed immersion (Ext^1=Hom(I/I^2,G)), empty scheme. Batch-5: lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model is a generic ring-theoretic comparison; its full closure has no nt-assume, Poincaré or trace-transport node, and neither assumption gives it, so the citation is accepted. All 13 declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. Maintainer note: Q119 delivered the same item in parallel (base cfb525d, one minute later); only one of the two should be merged.
